Study Notes, Evidence & Decision Logic

This tab holds the CFO-facing rationale behind the FAS dashboard. The default tab stays scan-ready for executives; this page documents source logic, governance gates, AI/ML assumptions, and the reasoning behind the decision-support operating design.

Why Page 1 First
  • Start with fiscal survival: FY25 deficit signal, FY26 close risk, and reserve runway must be locked before deeper workflow analysis.
  • Block false comfort: favorable May timing variance should not be released until accruals, commitments, and reforecast rows clear.
  • Govern the baseline: capital draws, donor-cash recognition, and tuition assumptions require explicit CFO gates.
AI/ML Use Boundary
  • Decision support only: AI/ML scores prioritize review order and scenario bands; they do not approve spending or recognize cash.
  • Required validation: HART / OAS / Workday rows, Controller stamp, and dean context must precede action.
  • Refresh cadence: monthly after close, weekly for red units during FY26 close and FY27 budget build.
Merge Logic
  • Decision shell retained: decision dashboard, evidence tab, clickable register chips, and CFO action-room flow.
  • FAS content retained: $1.8B stewardship model, divisional/department layers, HES revenue, research ICR, and capital backlog.
  • Best fit: executive scan first, methodology second, raw source rows available through export buttons.

CFO interpretation
  • Do not treat a favorable May variance as available cash.
  • Separate close timing, true savings, and structural base-budget issues.
  • Convert each red signal into a decision memo, not another dashboard view.
Governance rule
  • Restricted funds require donor-intent and legal release review.
  • Capital backlog requires risk-ranked triage before reserve draw.
  • Net tuition proposals must show true yield after aid.
Operating cadence
  • Red issues: weekly until source rows clear.
  • Amber issues: biweekly through FY26 close.
  • Green/favorable: hold centrally until Controller close validation.

FAS Mission Protection — CFO Crisis Decision Cockpit
Protect Teaching · Research · Access
Mission-Critical Decision Lens
Which commitments should be protected, delayed, redesigned, or funded differently under stress?
This section translates financial strain into mission-protection choices for FAS: protect teaching continuity, student access, sponsored research integrity, and core academic capacity while avoiding irreversible cuts or unauditable fixes.
Mission Gate 1 · Teaching Continuity
Course Cover
Protect required curriculum and high-enrollment service courses. Decision evidence: vacancy coverage, lecturer dependency, section demand, and semester-critical commitments.
Mission Gate 2 · Student Access
$12.2M
Keep aid pressure visible as a mission-protection item, not just a variance. Decision evidence: recurring aid driver, one-time bridge need, and FY27 base implication.
Mission Gate 3 · Research Continuity
$42.7M
Protect compliant research activity before the grant cliff becomes a payroll or lab-disruption problem. Decision evidence: sponsor terms, ICR yield, bridge eligibility, and close timing.
Mission Gate 4 · Academic Capacity
$50.6M
Convert vacancy savings into deliberate capacity choices. Decision evidence: criticality tier, service risk, backfill trigger, and whether savings are timing or structural.
Mission OutcomeCFO Signal to WatchDecision Support NeededRisk If Delayed

CFO View

In a crisis, the dashboard should not simply rank cuts. It should distinguish liquidity protection from mission damage, and show where a delay, redesign, bridge, or release decision best preserves FAS’s academic mission.

Automated CFO Contingency Triggers
Policy overrides that activate before the downside result drains operating cash.

⚡ Trigger 1 · CPI Capital Brake

  • Threshold: regional CPI crosses 4.0% for two consecutive quarters.
  • Action: freeze Tier 2 infrastructure draws from the $244M backlog pool and downgrade projects to Tier 3.
  • Purpose: eliminate capital operating shocks before reserves fall further.

⚡ Trigger 2 · Federal ICR Circuit Breaker

  • Threshold: monthly ICR receipts below $12M for more than 45 days.
  • Action: close the $8.4M research bridge pool to new applicants immediately.
  • Purpose: preserve remaining operating cash while Recovery Desk clears backlog.

⚡ Trigger 3 · Unlock Sprint Accelerator

  • Threshold: unrestricted liquidity drops below 40 days cash.
  • Action: merge Donor Sprint Phases 3 and 4.
  • Purpose: accelerate $22.4M vacant-chair endowment offsets into eligible salary relief.

📊 CFO Analyst Read — FY26 Close Posture
Hold the variance: The $20M favorable YTD position is predominantly timing-driven (vacancies, grant ramp delays). Bank it as contingency until June close accruals are complete — do not release for discretionary use.
Physics is the most acute risk: Third consecutive year of overrun; requires chair-level intervention, capital exception, and immediate postdoc-start freeze. Without action, this becomes a structural item in FY27.
Financial aid is the largest single exposure: The $12.2M above-plan demand is partly structural (affordability commitments) and partly enrollment-mix driven. Reforecast must be completed before FY27 budget is locked.
ICR recovery desk is the fastest revenue lever: Federal award timing creates a recoverable gap — but only with weekly billing, bridge-funding protocols, and active award reactivation coordination.

Net Tuition Compression — CFO Priority

Harvard College's financial aid commitment (no-loan policy, family contribution caps) means aid demand structurally tracks above gross tuition growth. Without the HES enrollment surge ($26M above plan), FY26 net tuition would be negative vs FY25. The CFO should model HES enrollment growth as a primary revenue lever and ensure all growth scenarios are tested before FY27 tuition rate decisions.
Aid Compression Risk
  • Current rate: 58.3% discount rate.
  • Peer lens: below the 61.4% peer median, but rising.
  • Trend: up from 54.1% in FY22 — a 4.2pp shift.
  • CFO read: net yield erosion needs FY27 reforecast attention.
HES as Strategic Lever
  • Volume: 14,812 enrolled versus 14,200 plan.
  • Revenue impact: $26M above plan — largest favorable FY26 offset.
  • Sensitivity: each additional 1,000 enrollments adds about $3.5M net revenue.
  • CFO read: scale with mission-fit and quality guardrails.
Restricted Aid Offset
  • Lever: restricted endowment funds earmarked for financial aid.
  • Budget effect: offsets pressure without gross tuition increases.
  • Method: donor-purpose review, legal use validation, spend-plan approval.
  • CFO read: prioritize aid-eligible endowments in the unlock sprint.

Capital Triage Requirement — Board Cycle Preparation

The $842M deferred maintenance backlog must be triaged before the next Board cycle using four criteria: (1) life safety and code compliance, (2) research and teaching mission continuity, (3) escalation risk (problems that grow faster the longer they wait), and (4) reserve impact. Emergency repairs that escape capital governance and hit the operating budget — like the $12M FY25 emergency HVAC spend — are the primary risk to avoid.
Emergency Repair Risk
  • FY25 impact: $12M emergency operating expense.
  • Root cause: deferred maintenance shifted planned capital work into emergency repair.
  • Recurrence risk: high without reserve policy and triage framework.
  • CFO read: convert emergency repairs into governed capital prioritization.
Reserve Draw Threshold
  • Reserve balance: $124M.
  • CFO threshold: below the $150M planning minimum.
  • Stress case: two simultaneous emergency repairs could impair routine capital planning.
  • CFO read: set reserve draw rules before the next Board cycle.
Space Optimization Opportunity
  • Cost signal: research labs cost $184/sqft/year.
  • Benchmark: more than 4× classroom-space cost.
  • Action: audit utilization across 40+ departments.
  • CFO read: labs below 60% utilization create consolidation, maintenance, and energy savings options.

CPA Audit & Financial Review

This section separates management forecasting from independent-auditor evidence: net asset classification, revenue recognition, internal controls over financial reporting, accrual review, Form 990 sensitivity, and OGC clearance for restricted funds.

CPA Risk Read
  • Primary issue: dashboard is strong operationally, but audit evidence must be hardened.

Dual-Ledger Bridge

  • Add: HART GL reconciliation bridge with source, owner, period, and sign-off fields.
  • Rule: leadership values require Controller group stamp.
OGC Clearance Path
  • Priority: restricted fund legal clearance unlocks actual liquidity.
  • Target: $48.2M fund portfolio segmented into four legal channels.
  • Next gate: Tier A go/no-go within 5 business days.

Dean Escalation Packet
Minimum facts needed to direct the issue to the right divisional dean.
  • Issue: department, fund, function, and threshold crossed.
  • Evidence: HART GL source row, OAS scenario, owner note, deadline.
  • Financial exposure: current amount, forecast run-rate, and cash impact.
  • Action requested: freeze, cap, reforecast, reconcile, or legal review.
  • Consequence: what happens if the division waits until close.

Priority 1
FY26 Close & FY27 Budget Lock
Controller + Director of Budget & Planning
Critical · June–July 2026
$20M contingency
Hold FY26 favorability in contingency until final close. Lock FY27 guidance using actual close evidence. Unreconciled funds and late accruals can make the CFO release savings too early.
Priority 2
Rolling 4-Quarter Reforecast Model
Budget & Planning + OAS Data Team
Build · Aug–Oct 2026
Framework
Annual-only budget review is too slow for federal funding, aid, and capital shocks. Approve driver-based quarterly reforecast with variance thresholds and department submission calendar.
Priority 3
Research Continuity & ICR Recovery Desk
Research Admin + Sponsored Finance
Urgent · June–Nov 2026
$16.2M ICR gap
Stand up weekly ICR collection, award activation, bridge-funding, and closeout review. Federal award timing can reverse favorable operating variance late in the year.
Priority 4
Faculty/Staff Workforce Financial Model
FAS Finance + HR + Divisional Deans
Priority · Sep–Dec 2026
$941M personnel base
Personnel costs are structurally sticky and crowd out research, aid, and capital flexibility. Approve a 5-year headcount and compensation model with mission-critical hiring gates.
Priority 5
Capital Reserve & Deferred Maintenance Triage
Facilities Finance + Capital Planning
Priority · Sep–Nov 2026
$842M backlog
Prioritize life-safety, research continuity, accessibility, and highest-risk deferred-maintenance projects. A single building failure can consume operating contingency mid-year.
Priority 6
Tuition, Aid & Net Revenue Model
College/GSAS Finance + Enrollment + Aid
Board Prep · Oct–Jan
$130M net tuition
Gross tuition decisions mislead if aid demand and enrollment mix are not modeled together. Present net revenue, aid sensitivity, and restricted-aid offsets before FY28 rate decisions.
Priority 7
Restricted Fund & Donor-Intent Review
FAS Finance + Development + Counsel
Opportunity · Jul–Dec 2026
$48.2M potential
Classify funds by legal purpose, utilization, age, and plausible expanded-use path. Large restricted balances can mask low spendable flexibility while the operating budget is under pressure.
